tags.qa_note: Re-audit 2026-08-02: depth and tidal-window figures vary across sources (PADI cites 40m max with exits at 22-25m; fiji.travel describes the wall extending 15-65m; diveotion.com and taveunidiveresort.com both independently confirm a ~2-4 day/month neap-tide accessible window, while PADI's general profile describes it as diveable most days with shifting entry times). Conflict documented in markdown rather than resolved by guessing.
Re-audit 2026-08-02: re-pulled all three sources, claims still hold. dive-the-world.com additionally confirms leopard sharks at this site (added to markdown, source-attributed).

DOWNGRADED 2026-08-02: previously validated on 2026-05-25 citing fijisharkdive.com, fijitravel.org, dive-the-world.com, but re-audit found none of the three actually names a 'Coral Gardens' site in Beqa Lagoon on direct re-fetch today. fijisharkdive.com/coral-dives lists Carpet Cove, Caesar's Rock, and Rusi's Pinnacle (not Coral Gardens). fijitravel.org's Beqa Lagoon site list is Shark Reef Marine Reserve, Caesar's Rocks, The Cathedral, Frigate Passage, North Save-a-Tack Passage, Big W. dive-the-world.com's Beqa Lagoon page lists Caesar's Rocks, Carpet Cove, E.T., Fantasea, Seven Sisters, The Pinnacle, Three Nuns. A WebSearch found a 'Coral Gardens' documented near Namotu Island in the Mamanuca Islands - a different destination entirely, echoing the same cross-region name-collision pattern already flagged for Supermarket Namena. Cannot confirm this is a genuinely distinct, named Beqa Lagoon site with 3 independent sources. Depth/difficulty are left as plausible defaults for a shallow lagoon site but are not source-confirmed.

MAJOR CORRECTION 2026-08-02: previous description (natural swim-through cavern with light beams, batfish, gorgonian-fringed roof, site_type=cave) was NOT supported by re-pulled sources. diveplanit.com (two separate pages), diveworldwide.com, and fijihigh.com independently describe 'The Cathedral' in the Beqa Lagoon/Pacific Harbour area as a structured shark-viewing dive at a rock/stone wall barrier ('viewing ledges'), featuring bull sharks (up to 30), occasional tiger sharks (1-3), grey/blacktip/whitetip reef sharks, lemon and nurse sharks, at 20-30m depth - not a natural cavern. Operator attribution is itself inconsistent across sources (diveplanit attributes it to Beqa Lagoon Resort; fijihigh.com attributes it to Beqa Adventure Divers) - this is flagged as unresolved in the markdown rather than guessed. fijitravel.org's original 'natural cavern with light beams and batfish' description could not be corroborated by any other source checked and is noted as a conflicting, unconfirmed account rather than presented as fact. site_type changed cave -> reef; difficulty changed Intermediate -> Advanced given the shark-feeding character consistent with Shark Reef Marine Reserve's rating.
